author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing shows the first page when asked for a page below one
summary: Opening the owner listing with a page value below 1 (0 or negative) renders the error page today. The owner listing must instead treat any page value below 1 as the first page and respond with the normal listing (HTTP 200).
acceptance_criteria: given a page value of 0, when /owners is requested, then the response is HTTP 200 and renders the normal owner listing showing the first page of results, not the error page
given a negative page value (e.g. -1), when /owners is requested, then the response is HTTP 200 and renders the same first page of the owner listing, not the error page
given a page value of 1 or above, when /owners is requested, then the listing behaves exactly as it does today (no regression to existing paging)
non_goals: Non-numeric page values (e.g. page=abc): the intake quotes only values below 1; their handling stays open
Page values beyond the last page of results: not named in the intake; behavior stays as today
Changing page size, sort order, or the pagination controls
Paging on the veterinarian directory: the intake names only the owner listing
notes: Observed cause (for the implementer to confirm under TDD): OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) from the raw page parameter, and a negative page index is rejected, which surfaces as the error page. Per docs/architecture-principles.md (Web controller row), normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule. The 0 and negative cases are one behavior: cover them with one data-driven test. The current-page indicator in the rendered listing should read as the first page. docs/prd.md already carries REQ-OWN-005 (narrative sentence, anchor, Done-when bullet) in the uncommitted tree; no Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by docs/architecture-principles.md § Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the clamp belongs in OwnerController (Contracts row OwnerController, now also implementing REQ-OWN-005). Cause confirmed by grep (weaker basis, no IDE oracle): OwnerController.processFindForm binds `page` raw, and findPaginatedForOwnersLastName passes `page - 1` to PageRequest.of, which rejects a negative index. Fix: clamp the bound page to a minimum of 1 once, at the top of processFindForm, and use that normalized value for both the Pageable and the `currentPage` model attribute, so the listing's current-page indicator reads as the first page. No new type, module, or pattern is needed.
integration_points: Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): use the test class's existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository fixture, which is a framework stub. A hand-written double would mean replacing the shared @WebMvcTest fixture for the whole class, which is outside this slice. Stub findByLastNameStartingWith to return a multi-owner page so the listing view renders. Capture the Pageable to assert page index 0, or assert model attribute currentPage == 1.

Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned HTTP stand-in (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy). Cover the 0 and negative cases with one data-driven test, theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage, asserting status 200, view owners/ownersList, and currentPage 1. The existing page=1 tests (processFindFormSuccess and others) cover the no-regression criterion.

Binding target for GET /owners: unchanged. The `page` value is bound to a request-scoped int @RequestParam. Owner binding stays as it is today, under the existing @InitBinder disallowed-fields list. No new entry point.

patterns.description: Parameter range normalization is binding and lives in the controller; it is not a new business-rule deviation.

risks.risk: Owner listing query scales with owner count. docs/system-design.md has no § Scale and Load section, so no row exists to cite.
risks.mitigation: The slice adds no path and does not change the query. Page size stays fixed (system-design § Constants note), so the path is bounded and the fix should take the simplest readable form, a Math.max-style clamp.

risks.risk: currentPage stays raw (0 or -1) while the query is clamped, so the pagination controls render an out-of-range current page.
risks.mitigation: Clamp once and feed the same value to both the query and the model (prd-entry notes).

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Design write: REQ-OWN-005 joined the OwnerController Contracts row in docs/system-design.md; this is the only docs/ edit. VetController has the same `page - 1` shape, and the prd-entry declares it a non-goal; it is not touched. Brief gap for the owner: docs/system-design.md lacks the § Scale and Load section the design-validation checklist expects. No row is written here because this slice adds no data-scaling path.

The second owner is irrelevant to the behavior and only has to make the page hold more than one owner.
findings.fix: Add a named default factory for an irrelevant owner (e.g. `anOwner()`) and use it at line 156. Leave the older tests as they are.

recommendations: The literal 1 in model().attribute("currentPage", 1) is the first-page value the test is about, so it is acceptable. A named constant such as FIRST_PAGE would read better but is optional.

The stubbed Pageable matches any(Pageable.class), so the zero-based page index is never asserted directly. Failure on a negative index and the currentPage check cover the risk, so no further assertion is needed.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Input validation at the trust boundary: the request-supplied page is clamped right where it enters the handler, OwnerController.java:97 `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, 1);`, before it reaches `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` at OwnerController.java:134. That removes the negative-index IllegalArgumentException path that used to render the error page. It also matches the neighboring boundary normalization of lastName (`lastName = lastName.strip();`, OwnerController.java:104). Pattern consistency holds.

No removed or weakened control: the only production hunk renames the parameter, adds `name = "page"` and keeps `defaultValue = "1"`. A non-numeric page still fails int conversion in the framework, as before. The `@InitBinder` disallow list `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");` (OwnerController.java:61) is unchanged.

No injection or XSS surface: the normalized int reaches only the Spring Data derived query `findByLastNameStartingWith` through a Pageable and the `currentPage` model attribute (an int, rendered through default Thymeleaf escaping). No query text, path, template expression or log line uses request input in this diff.
Upper bound not widened: a very large page still yields an empty or not-found result, as it did before this change, so there is no new allocation or reach.

No secrets in the diff: grep -i -E 'password|secret|token|apikey|api_key' over the changeset output returned no matches. The diff adds no endpoint and does not touch build.gradle or the dependency set.

Supply chain: build.gradle configures no OWASP dependency-check (grep -n -i 'dependencyCheck|owasp' build.gradle returned nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review. ./gradlew dependencies (runtimeClasspath) resolves org.springframework.boot:spring-boot:4.1.1 and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind:3.1.5.
